main_text.p: Maiorem probat his verbis: O altaria tua, Rex mi, & Deus mi)
1. Quibuscunq; hic finis propositus est Dei cultu religiose perfungi, ij digni sunt qui non impediatur in sacro hoc instituto.
Mihi altaria tua cordi sunt. Hoc est, Ego sacrificia laudis offerendo, & cultum debitum tibi praestando, officio meo satisfacere cupio.
Non igitur mihi remorae sancti instituti, injiciendae sunt.
2. Nihil dubium est meliorem esse debere conditionem eorum, quos Deus no creauit tantum, sed etiam de hoc mundo sanctificatos redemit, & gubernat.
Atqui pafferes & hirudines Deus creauit solum: me etiā redemit & gubernat. Ideo enim Deum meum & Regem meum, meri toipsius maximo, nuncupare debeo.
Debebat igitur conditio mea melior esse. Stat enim illud: Beatus est populus cuius Iehouah est Deus. Psal. 144. 15.
Nos quoties idem affectus nobis cordi est, cum eodem nostro Psalmographo Dominū precemur: Educ e carcere animam meam, ut celebrem nomen tuum: me coronabunt iusti, quod conditionem meam commutaris.

page.notes: Marginal reading: the running head is "COMMENTARIA." The page number is printed as "183" (the 8 and the 3 are clear; the last numeral is an old-style form). Several words in the scan are worn or blurred and were read as printed; the following may be doubtful: "nō" (non), "remoræ", "pafferes" (passeres, as printed), "meri" (mei), "toipsius", "cupio". The line "Mihi altaria tua" and the Psalm references are printed in the body. The line "M 4 VER-" at the foot is a catchword-like fragment with a signature mark "M 4"; it is kept as a paragraph. Printed Greek or Hebrew: none visible. Hyphenation at line end in "VER-" is printed. Uncertain: "Non igitur mihi remorae fancti instituti" reads as "sancti" in the scan but is set as "fancti" with a long-s-like f; transcribed as printed with the spelling as seen. Transcription is approximate for the worn passages and should be checked against the scan.
